introduction.text: The Forum Boarium was the ancient Roman cattle market and commercial hub located near the Tiber in Rome. It played a key role in the city’s trade, religious life, and early gladiatorial spectacles.

history.description: The Ara Maxima, a massive altar, was erected on the site in the 6th or 5th century BC.
The first recorded gladiatorial contest in Rome took place at the Forum Boarium in 264 BC.
In 215 BC, four people were buried alive under the Forum Boarium as human sacrifices.
The Temple of Hercules Victor was constructed in the 2nd century BC.
The Temple of Portunus was built between 100 and 80 BC.
During the late Western Roman Empire, the Forum Boarium area was converted into a commercial district with shops.
Conservation work on the temples and landscaping began in the late 1990s.

design.description: The Temple of Hercules Victor is a circular peristyle building with a colonnade of Corinthian columns arranged in a concentric ring around a cylindrical cella.
The Temple of Portunus is a rectangular structure with a tetrastyle Ionic portico and a cella on a podium, built of tuff and travertine.
Restoration efforts have preserved the temples and introduced new landscaping to the Forum Boarium site.

art.description: A statue by the sculptor Myron, possibly depicting Theseus defeating the Minotaur, was once placed at the Forum Boarium.
